what: Henri IV to Bellièvre and Sillery at Vervins, 14 March (Angers), 9 April (Angers) and 14 April 1598 (Nantes); originals signed Henry with passages in a figure-letter-sign cipher, about 90 lines in all, no decipherment on the leaves
why_not: The full clear text of all three despatches is printed from the Court's copies (BnF Béthune 8972, Brienne 66 according to Berger de Xivrey) in Mémoires et correspondance de Duplessis-Mornay, t. VIII, 1824 (archive.org mmoiresetcorresp08morn): 14 March = letter LXX, pp. 162-175 (the clear sentences on either side of the f. 241v cipher block are on pp. 173-174 with the enciphered sentences between them); 9 April = letter CXIX, pp. 290-304 (ends as f. 285r does); 14 April = letter CXXV, pp. 317-320 (the f. 302r cipher begins after 'en attendant la conclusion', which the print continues 'du traicté, pour lequel vous estes par delà'). Verdict would be 'read' (plaintext in print), not 'open'.
use: Known-plaintext pairs for the 1598 Court cipher with the Vervins plenipotentiaries (key recovery from external plaintext); not found on Tomokiyo's henryiv.htm (no mention of Vervins or fr. 15911).
